title: Himalayan 750 to be unveiled at EICMA: What we Know
text:
Himalayan 750 to be unveiled at EICMA: What we Know - BikeWale 
 Log In AD Himalayan 750 to be unveiled at EICMA: What we Know
 Siddharth Govindarajan October 28, 2026, 09:00 PM IST 24,162 Views Royal Enfield has teased the Himalayan 750 on social media ahead of its official unveiling. The teaser shows a silhouette of the Himalayan 750 against a scarlet sky accompanied by coordinates that point to central Milan. This all but confirms RE's first parallel-twin adventure tourer will be revealed at the EICMA exhibition held between 3 and 6 November.
 Himalayan 750 is a significant model for Royal Enfield for multiple reasons. It will be the first bike bearing the Himalayan moniker to get a parallel-twin engine and the first in RE's range built on the new 750cc platform. While we await the official unveiling at EICMA, here's what we know about the new Himalayan 750.
 750cc parallel-twin engine 
 The Himalayan 750 will come with Royal Enfield's new 750cc oil-cooled parallel-twin engine. Riders have been yearning for a more powerful engine in the Himalayan ever since the original 411 nearly ten years ago. Himalayan 450 has been a significant step in the right direction; the itch clearly hasn't been scratched fully. The new engine is expected to produce approximately 55 to 60bhp, while torque figures are expected to be around the 65Nm mark.
 The new engine will retain the 270-degree firing order from its predecessor resulting in a mean bark from the 2-into-1, high-mounted single exhaust. Himalayan 750 will also receive a six-speed manual gearbox with a complementary slip-and-assist clutch working in tandem.
 New chassis, multiple wheel sizes 
 Royal Enfield currently uses a double down-tube setup on its 650 twins and a steel twinspar tubular frame on the Himalayan 450, yet the Himalayan 750 is expected to differ from both. While exact details are still unknown, the Himalayan 750 will be positioned as a road-biased tourer with less of an off-road focus than the Himalayan 450. 750 is also expected to get a 19/17-inch front/rear wheel setup with the choice between alloy or spoked wheels depending on the variant selected.
 Better suspension and braking setup 
 For suspension, the Himalayan 750 will use a Showa upside-down (USD) fork at the front. Opting for a USD fork over a conventional right-side-up (RSU) remains consistent with the Himalayan 750's positioning as a road-biased machine. Also, in a first for Royal Enfield, the Himalayan 750 features twin disc brakes at the front with ByBre callipers.
 The front suspension is expected to be adjustable for preload and compression. As will the Showa linked rear monoshock, which we observed comes with a remote preload adjuster. This should help make adjustments on the fly with a pillion or luggage mounted on the bike.
 Circular TFT instrument cluster 
 The Himalayan 750 will get the 4-inch circular full-colour TFT display shared with the Himalayan 450 and the Bear 650 scrambler. We know how good this unit is on the aforementioned motorcycles; it will be interesting to see how it fares on the Himalayan 750. The cluster comes with full-screen Google Maps mirroring and call/music control with Bluetooth connectivity. Adjacent to the instrument cluster will also be a Type-C USB charging port.
 Cruise control, switchable ABS, and ride modes 
 Rider convenience and safety technology is an area where the Himalayan 750 is set to distinguish itself from Royal Enfield's other offerings. In a first for the Chennai-based automaker, the Himalayan 750 will come with factory-equipped cruise control and a tyre-pressure monitoring system (TPMS).
 The system can be toggled through a switch on the right-hand-side handlebar grip and the set speed can also be adjusted without needing to disengage the system. This ride-by-wire system will also offer traction control and multiple ride modes to alter the throttle response to suit various conditions. The Himalayan 750 will also feature dual-channel ABS, while the rear may be switchable for more spirited off-road riding.
 Royal Enfield's Himalayan 750 will be one of the most hotly anticipated launches at EICMA. The India launch for the Himalayan 750 may occur later this month at Royal Enfield's annual MotorFest event, happening between 24 and 26 November.
 The Himalayan 750 will be available in a choice of at least four colours, while pricing is expected to be around the Rs. 4.50 to 5.00 lakh mark (ex-showroom).
